note: Round 1 taxonomy from 859 search-result titles. A pain is a problem the room states, not a topic. Keys are used in labels/*.jsonl.

pains.label: My verbal score is stuck. RC, vocab and sentence completion don't improve, and word lists make me procrastinate.
pains.definition: A member says their GRE verbal score is low or not improving (scores around 140-150), they struggle with reading comprehension, vocabulary, sentence completion or verbal timing, or they fear a low verbal score will get them rejected.

pains.label: Confused between Jamboree, Princeton Review (Manya), Dilip Oak and the rest. Which coaching centre in my city is worth the fees?
pains.definition: A member asks which GRE coaching institute, online course or tutor to pay for, compares named institutes, asks a centre's fees, or reviews a paid coaching. The decision is which paid option, not whether to pay at all.

pains.label: Do I really need coaching, or can I crack the GRE on my own?
pains.definition: A member asks whether coaching is necessary or worth the money, or asks how to prepare without joining any institute.

pains.label: Which books, sites, apps or mocks should I follow? Too many options, don't know which to trust.
pains.definition: A member asks for the best books, online resources, apps, mock tests or study material for self-preparation, or which of several sources to follow.

pains.label: The fee is ₹22,550 (or $205, or is it 205 rupees?). Why so high? What does a retake, reschedule or extra score report cost?
pains.definition: A member asks or complains about the GRE registration fee in India, whether to pay in dollars or rupees, the cost of a second attempt, rescheduling, cancellation, score reports, waivers or other hidden costs.

pains.label: I got 300-313 and I'm not satisfied. Is it enough, or should I pay to sit again?
pains.definition: A member reports a score they are unhappy with (typically 300-315, or a weak section score) and asks whether it is enough or whether to retake, or fears that a low score shuts them out.

pains.label: I work 9-5 with a commute and huge work pressure. How do I fit GRE prep into 2 months?
pains.definition: A working professional asks how to prepare for the GRE alongside a full-time job, or shares how they managed it.

pains.label: I'm in BTech (or just finished). When should I start, is it tough, and what do I do first?
pains.definition: A beginner, usually a BTech student, asks when to start preparing, whether the GRE is tough, what the exam is like, or simply 'tell me what I do'.

pains.label: GRE or GATE (or CAT)? MS abroad, MTech in India, or just keep the job?
pains.definition: A member weighs the GRE against GATE, CAT or a job; the path decision that comes before paying for GRE prep.

pains.label: Universities are waiving the GRE. Is it compulsory for MS in the US? Is it worth taking at all now?
pains.definition: A member asks whether the GRE is required or worth taking, given waivers and GRE-optional programs, or says the GRE has become pointless.

pains.label: Take it at home or at a centre? Setup, ID rules, surprises on the day, and the cheating crackdown on Indian at-home takers.
pains.definition: A member asks whether to sit the at-home GRE or a test centre, or shares an at-home experience with problems or surprises; media about at-home cheating and bans in India.

pains.label: I paid for coaching or an online course and it did not help. Now I want a refund.
pains.definition: A member reports paying a GRE coaching institute or course that was a waste, or fights for a refund. Round 1 found little of this in titles; it is kept so later rounds can look for it.

pains.label: Got the score but a low GPA (or the reverse). Which universities match my profile? Someone evaluate my profile.
pains.definition: A member asks which universities to apply to with a given GRE score and profile, asks for a profile evaluation, or asks what else beyond the GRE an admit needs.

pains.label: Which agency for university selection, SOP, LOR and visa: Manya, Jamboree, Leap Scholar, The Chopras?
pains.definition: A member asks which admissions counsellor or agency to pay for the application process, or asks for reviews of one.
